question: Should OpenClaw add a persisted `tools.exec.shell` override, and what approval, safe-bin, PATH, WSL, node, sandbox, and validation boundaries must that contract enforce?
rationale: This choice changes the interpreter for command execution, so code inspection alone cannot decide the product/security contract or whether the added config surface is acceptable.

options.title: Keep open for a full shell contract
options.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical tracker and require a design that covers config precedence, shell arguments, validation, WSL path handling, approval semantics, safe-bin trust, node, sandbox, PTY, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Limit work to narrow Windows fixes
options.body: Defer arbitrary shell configuration and only land focused fixes such as PowerShell 7 PATH resolution when they preserve existing exec security boundaries.

options.title: Reject persisted shell override
options.body: Close the feature direction and document supported workarounds or a different extension point for users who need alternate shells.

recommendation.title: Keep open for a full shell contract
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical tracker and require a design that covers config precedence, shell arguments, validation, WSL path handling, approval semantics, safe-bin trust, node, sandbox, PTY, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across PowerShell selection, exec config precedent, and host exec environment hardening for this decision surface.
